coco-si.meta_description: Each of the 495 requires a live, checkable source. Then 229 skills ship what they decided.
coco-si.how_sub: Each of the 495 requires a live, checkable source. Then 229 skills ship what they decided.
coco-si.panel_note: Install with npx cocosuperintelligence. Files and state stay on your machine, with no telemetry and your own model keys.
steps: Install in one command
Run npx cocosuperintelligence to clone the pinned v1.10.0 release tag and wire your coding agent.
Convene the board
Ask a hard question with /SI-Decide; specialists across 13 departments argue in rounds and record dissent by name.
Execute with skills and agents
Hand the decision to 229 skills, 388 customer-facing commands and 34 specialist agents inside Claude Code, Cursor or Codex.
coco-si.rules_sub: Every persona requires checkable public sources, quotes are labelled reconstructions, and core tooling is Apache-2.0.
rules: Disagreement is recorded by name instead of smoothed into a generic consensus summary.
Coco installs into your local tool directories and uses the model provider you already configure.
Most of the framework is Apache-2.0; the Super Intelligence persona board is proprietary.
specs: 34. 10 core, plus 24 in the GSD bundle.
495 across 13 departments, each behind an evidence-validation gate.
16 adapters across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Grok Build and AGENTS.md tools.
6 default bundles: GSD, HyperFrames, Super Intelligence, Brain, M0 and Cognee.
Open-core: core framework under Apache-2.0; Super Intelligence board proprietary.

what_it_is.tagline: An advisory board of expert personas inside the coding tool you already use.
what_it_is.paragraph: Coco Super Intelligence seats an advisory board of expert personas inside the coding tool you already use, returns one pick with the dissent named, then does the work through local skills, commands and agents.

capabilities.title: 16 to 32 personas on /SI-Decide
capabilities.desc: Ask one hard question with /SI-Decide and it seats 16 to 32 of 495 personas across 13 departments; add --debate for reaction rounds before the vote.

capabilities.title: Cited public stances and stance check
capabilities.desc: Every persona answers from cited public stances, and a stance check flags anything that does not trace to a source.

capabilities.title: 229 skills, 388 commands and 34 agents
capabilities.desc: Ships 229 skills, 388 commands and 34 agents; a default Claude Code install delivers 191 of the skills.

capabilities.title: One-command install across 16 tools
capabilities.desc: One command, npx cocosuperintelligence, installs into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code and 12 other coding tools (16 adapters).

capabilities.title: Phase state saved across chats
capabilities.desc: Writes phase state to disk, so a cleared chat does not erase the plan.

capabilities.title: Local files, no telemetry, your own keys
capabilities.desc: Files stay on your machine, with no telemetry; your coding tool keeps its own model provider and keys.

capabilities.title: Clean manifest uninstall
capabilities.desc: --uninstall removes only what the install recorded and restores your original files.

cooking.title: Coco MCP server for any MCP-capable tool
cooking.desc: A local stdio MCP server so any MCP-capable coding tool can call Coco's skills, commands, agents and persona board, with one-step harness setup.

cooking.title: Skills that improve themselves
cooking.desc: An unattended loop scores each change against held-out tests and keeps only the ones that win, with an off switch.

cooking.title: Offline persona source checker
cooking.desc: An offline persona checker that tests every persona's sources before it joins the board, so the board can grow without losing its citations.

stage.desc: Released and in daily use: v1.10.0 on npm, the 10th of 10 milestone releases (v1.0.0 through v1.10.0). v2.0 is next.

voice.how_sub: Coco Voice runs the acoustic and speech-to-text model directly on your hardware, turning spoken thoughts into clean text wherever your cursor sits.
voice.panel_note: No account, no subscription and no remote API key required. Once the model weights are on disk, dictation works offline at full speed.
steps: Capture
Press your shortcut in any editor, terminal or browser window.
Transcribe on device
Local inference converts your voice on your own CPU and GPU without network calls.
Insert cleanly
Text lands straight at the cursor, keeping your focus inside the work.
voice.rules_sub: Every Coco Research product states what runs today, where data lives and how every model weight is checked.
rules: Voice recordings, transcripts and meeting notes stay on your own computer; there is no cloud relay.
Only MIT, Apache-2.0 and CC-BY-4.0 models are offered, and every download is checked against its pinned SHA-256.
Download ready-to-run releases or inspect and compile every line from the public repository.
voice.credits_html: Credits: Started as a fork of Handy by CJ Pais (Copyright (c) 2025 CJ Pais, MIT License); third-party notices in NOTICE.

what_it_is.tagline: Hold a key, speak, and your words are typed into the app you already have open.
what_it_is.paragraph: Coco Voice is private speech-to-text on your own computer: hold a key to dictate into the app you have open, tidy transcripts with a local model, and keep cited meeting notes on disk with no account and no subscription.

capabilities.title: Push-to-talk in any app, offline
capabilities.desc: Option+Space on macOS, Ctrl+Space on Windows and Linux, or toggle mode. Recognition works offline once your model is downloaded.

capabilities.title: Open speech models, SHA-256 checked
capabilities.desc: Pick your own open speech model, including Whisper, Parakeet and Moonshine. Each download shows its licence and is checked against a pinned SHA-256 before use.

capabilities.title: On-device clean-up and custom words
capabilities.desc: A local Qwen3-4B model on Mac tidies text and drops spoken self-corrections such as 'scratch that', alongside custom vocabulary and local history.

capabilities.title: Meeting notes core with segment citations
capabilities.desc: Version 0.11.0 stores meeting notes and notepad points locally on disk, with segment citations linking each note back to what was said.

capabilities.title: Private by design
capabilities.desc: Dictated text never goes into log files, app data stays private to your user account, the paste is skipped while macOS secure input is on, and if a paste fails the text stays on your clipboard.

capabilities.title: macOS, Windows and Linux installers
capabilities.desc: Installers for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows (x64 and ARM64) and Linux (AppImage, deb, rpm on x86_64 and arm64), plus a one-command install on Apple Silicon Macs and 22 UI languages.

cooking.title: Dedicated Meetings screens
cooking.desc: Dedicated desktop screens for live meeting recording controls, dual-track speaker view, and searchable meeting views.

cooking.title: Clean-up on out of the box
cooking.desc: Clean-up on out of the box, filler-word removal that follows the language you speak (and can be switched off), and history limits that do what they say.

cooking.title: Per-app profiles
cooking.desc: Tone, capitals and punctuation follow the app in front, and apps you block are never dictated into.

signal.how_title: A calm page where only what matters speaks.
signal.how_sub: Signal is Coco Research's open design language: three editions, CSS custom properties and written rules for interfaces that stay legible under real work.
signal.panel_note: Published as Apache-2.0-licensed CSS and documentation in the public repository, with no packaged npm release today.
steps: Semantic colour discipline
Colour encodes one state meaning at a time: action, progress, gap or failure.
Word and shape together
Every status pairs a readable label with a distinct geometric cue rather than colour alone.
Numbers with denominators
Counts appear alongside their total or baseline, in tabular numerals across light and dark themes.
signal.rules_sub: Every token in Signal exists to carry meaning rather than decoration.
rules: Shared typography, spacing proportions and contrast floors across light paper and dark stage views.
Plain stylesheets and static documentation with no tracking scripts.
Read, copy or audit the CSS and specification directly on GitHub.

what_it_is.tagline: Coco Research's open design language: three editions, CSS tokens and layout documentation.
what_it_is.paragraph: Signal defines the typographic scale, light paper and dark stage tokens, and semantic state rules used across Coco Research interfaces.

capabilities.title: Three editions, light and dark
capabilities.desc: Three editions with first-class light paper and dark stage tokens across desktop and phone viewports.

capabilities.title: Variable typography and tabular numerals
capabilities.desc: Archivo and Martian Mono variable typography scale with tabular numerals for counts and baselines.

capabilities.title: Zero runtime tracking or network calls
capabilities.desc: Static stylesheets and page scripts make zero runtime network requests, analytics beacons or tracking calls.

capabilities.title: Reduced-motion fallbacks
capabilities.desc: Native prefers-reduced-motion rules disable transitions and WebGL motion cleanly.

cooking.desc: Upcoming design-language items are not listed in the public repository yet.

mira.how_title: Reels and Shorts rendered on your own machine.
mira.how_sub: Mira is a Python pipeline for assembling vertical short-form videos in English and Hindi locally, without uploading raw drafts to a hosted editing studio.
mira.panel_note: Archived Python source repository under AGPL-3.0 on GitHub. There is no packaged installer or tagged binary release.
steps: Script in English or Hindi
Prepare vertical story beats and bilingual lines on your local filesystem.
Assemble media locally
Run the Python pipeline on your own hardware to pair audio timing, captions and visual frames.
Export vertical cuts
Write finished vertical video files straight to disk with no watermark or cloud queue.
mira.rules_sub: Mira ships as inspectable Python source code rather than a hosted SaaS service.
rules: Drafts, voice tracks and rendered vertical cuts stay in your local project folders.
Full Python source is public under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0.
Publicly archived source repository on GitHub; stage is stated plainly.

kns: Rules, adversary checks, budget and audit
loops.how_sub: Coco Loops wraps autonomous agent iterations in explicit rules, adversary verification checks, hard budget caps and an inspectable audit trail.
loops.panel_note: Source available on GitHub for inspection and local runs; no packaged release is published today.
steps: Bind rules and budget caps
Declare hard iteration limits, allowed paths and spend ceilings before a loop begins.
Run adversary checks
Each candidate change faces an independent check gate instead of self-certifying its own output.
Record the audit trail
Every turn writes its inputs, verdict and stop reason to a local log you can inspect.
loops.rules_sub: An unattended loop without a ceiling or independent check is not governance.
rules: Loops stop deterministically when a turn, token or failure threshold is reached.
Checks run against explicit criteria rather than trusting the proposer's own claim.
Public source repository today, with stage stated plainly.

what_it_is.tagline: Governance for autonomous agent loops: rules, adversary checks, budget caps and an audit trail.
what_it_is.paragraph: Coco Loops wraps autonomous agent iterations in deterministic budget ceilings, independent adversary checks, and an inspectable local audit trail.

Resolve target action

kns: Local live view on your machine
heliopause.how_title: Give your AI tools a Lead and roles on your machine.
heliopause.how_sub: Heliopause by Coco Research organizes local AI tools under a Lead and explicit roles, serving a live status board from local files over loopback.
heliopause.panel_note: Runs on Python's standard library bound strictly to local loopback, with zero external runtime dependencies, zero telemetry and zero remote sync.
steps: Assign a Lead and roles
Structure coding and research agents with clear responsibilities like a small local company.
Read local state files
See who is busy, what is moving and what waits on your call without leaving your machine.
Serve on loopback only
Inspect the live Signal board in your local browser with nothing exposed to the network.
heliopause.rules_sub: Heliopause by Coco Research is source-available under Apache-2.0 as an early preview.
rules: The local server listens only on your own machine; there is no cloud dashboard or remote sync.
Built on the Python standard library so every line you run is easy to audit.
Public v0.7.3 release and source repository on GitHub, with stage stated plainly.
